notes.title: July 2025 Update: Keystroke capture, rounded camera, splash screen and more
notes.content: [p]July 2025 update, brings a feature to add keystrokes to the output video. This is a useful tool to make professional video tutorials.[/p][p] Watermark feature is now split into Text and Image, allowing you to add both image and text to the output.[/p][p]Additionally, you can now assign hotkeys to toggle camera and input/output audio. [i]Rounded Rectangle[/i] shape is also allowed to choose for camera image.[/p][p]There are more user interface improvements in this update, including a splash screen application startup to let you know that the app in loading, redesigned and improved icons, improved hotkey support and more.[/p][p]If you are interested in the details, check out the release notes on [url="https://www.screenbits.com/release-notes"]Screenbits website[/url]. [/p]

notes.title: May 2025 Update: New screen capture method, permissions and UI improvements
notes.content:
May 2025 update adds an option to use the new screen capture APIs in case of issues with the default method. By enabling [b]Prefer modern screen capture[/b] option from [b]Screen & pointer options[/b], new capture APIs (WGC) is used instead of the default (DXGI).

Additionally, Screenbits can now detect if Camera or Microphone are not accessible due to Windows Privacy settings. It prevents recording error and lets you know before recording starts.

A few UI improvements and bug fixes are also applied in this update.

If you are interested in the details, check out the release notes on [url=https://www.screenbits.com/release-notes ]Screenbits website[/url].

notes.title: February 2025 Update: Internal improvements and bug fixes
notes.content:
February 2025 update simply fixes a few bugs related to recording errors, capturing virtual cameras and overexposed screen capture output.

If you are interested in the details, check out the release notes on [url=https://www.screenbits.com/release-notes ]Screenbits website[/url].

notes.title: January 2025 Update: Auto-pause, mute/unmute and more
notes.content:
January 2025 update brings new features for scheduler, audio sources and hotkeys, and a few improvements for the user interface.

Scheduler now supports pause mode which enables automatic pause at certain time, duration or size of the output file. You can now mute/unmute audio sources from UI or using hotkeys, supporting push-to-talk and push-to-mute. Speaking of hotkeys, middle and extra mouse buttons can now be used for hotkeys.

As for the user interface improvements, you can now view name of the monitor for selected display and name of the application for selected window.

If you are interested in the details, check out the release notes on [url=https://www.screenbits.com/release-notes ]Screenbits website[/url].

notes.title: December 2024 Update: Improved window capture mode
notes.content:
December update improves [i]Window[/i] capture mode which allows capturing content of top level windows even if obscured by other windows. There are also improvements in pointer highlight effect and UI scaling on multi-display setups as well as a few bug fixes.

If you are interested in the details, check out the release notes on [url=https://www.screenbits.com/release-notes ]Screenbits website[/url].

notes.title: October 2024 Update: Performance improvements and bug fixes
notes.content:
October 2024 update improves performance of screen capturing and also the area selector. Additionally, as a little new feature, you can now flip camera image vertically. There are also multiple bug fixes which the most important one is fixing oversaturated screen capture from HDR enabled displays.

If you are interested in the details, check out the release notes on [url=https://www.screenbits.com/release-notes ]Screenbits website[/url].

notes.title: August 2024 Update: Performance improvements
notes.content:
August 2024 update brings performance improvements in screen and mouse pointer capturing, and also recording performance on Windows 11. Additionally, audio capturing quality is improved in this update.

If you are interested in the details, check out the release notes on [url=https://www.screenbits.com/release-notes ]Screenbits website[/url].

notes.title: July 2024 update: Audio meter and UI Improvements
notes.content:
July 2024 update adds audio meter to view audio levels for both input and output audio. This feature makes it easier to make sure if the app is capturing audio from the selected devices by checking the levels on the audio meter. Minor user interface improvements are also applied in this update.

If you are interested in the details, check out the release notes on [url=https://www.screenbits.com/release-notes ]Screenbits website[/url].

notes.title: April 2024 update: New media processing engine, audio and watermark options
notes.content:
April 2024 update brings a new media processing engine which improves recording performance. New audio and watermark options are also available in the update.

You can now change volume from the app for both system audio and the microphone. It can increase by up to 200% in case you need the sound to be louder for your recordings.  

An option is also added to turn off surround sound in order to get maximum volume (as you hear) for system audio in case you use a virtual surround headphone.

Watermark overlay gets more customization options in the update as you can now change text alignment and outline thickness for the watermark text.

If you are interested in the details, check out the release notes on [url=https://www.screenbits.com/release-notes ]Screenbits website[/url].

notes.title: August 2023 Update: AMD VCE for video encoding
notes.content:
August 2023 update fixes an issue related to AMD VCE for video encoding which was preventing the software to use the hardware encoder properly.

After this update, Screenbits should perform significantly better on AMD video cards so If you are using an AMD video card and wasn't happy with performance of the application, we recommend you give it a try after this update.

If you are interested in the details, check out the release notes on [url=https://www.screenbits.com/release-notes ]Screenbits website[/url].

notes.title: June 2023 Update: HEVC encoding, Window capture mode and area presets
notes.content:
June 2023 update brings the ability to choose HEVC hardware encoder (if available) for video encoding. It also adds a "Window" capture mode to simplify capturing window areas as you can now choose application windows from a list. Area presets are also available to save frequently used areas in Area capture mode and easily restore them at any time.

In addition to these features this update includes other improvements and bug fixes. If you are interested in the details, check out the release notes on [url=https://www.screenbits.com/release-notes ]Screenbits website[/url].

notes.title: February 2023 Update: Performance improvements
notes.content:
As we add new features to Screenbits through each update, we also want to make sure the app is working as expected and performing better and better within each update. 

February 2023 update brings significant performance improvements in hardware video encoding. Compared to the previous version, you may experience up to 50% less CPU usage if you use hardware acceleration for video encoding. This improves recording quality and framerate of the output video and also allows your system to dedicate more resources to other applications or the game which you play during recording.

In addition to this improvement, we have fixed a few bugs in the recent updates. If you are interested in the details, check out the release notes on [url=https://www.screenbits.com/release-notes ]Screenbits website[/url].

notes.title: December 2022 Update: Draw on Screen
notes.content:
December 2022 update brings Draw on Screen feature which allows you to write, draw and highlight anywhere on your screen! There are several tools such as pen, marker, arrow, rectangle and text to use for drawing.

If you are interested in the details, check out the release notes on [url=https://www.screenbits.com/release-notes ]Screenbits website[/url].

notes.title: July 2022 Update: Video encoding and camera options
notes.content:
March 2022 update brings an option to let users choose which hardware encoder should be used to encode video. This option replaces the previous one which only allowed users to choose if they want the application to use hardware to encode videos or not.

Since this update, you can also customize thickness of the border around camera overlay from camera options.

If you are interested in the details, check out the release notes on [url=https://www.screenbits.com/release-notes ]Screenbits website[/url].

notes.title: June 2022 Update: Compact View, Schedule, Custom Camera Graphics and more
notes.content:
June 2022 update brings new features including compact view, schedule, custom camera graphics and fractional frame rate.

Compact view provides a minimal user interface to interact with the app. You can use schedule feature to schedule recording to start at a certain time. In this update, you can also add custom graphics image to camera image to make it more fun. It is now possible to choose fractional frame rates (such as 29.97 or 30000/1001) for the output video.

There are also minor user interface improvements in this update. If you are interested in the details, check out the release notes on [url=https://www.screenbits.com/release-notes ]Screenbits website[/url].

notes.title: March 2022 Update: Bug fixes
notes.content:
As we add new features to Screenbits through regular and major updates, we also want to make sure the app is working as expected and performing better within each update. March 2022 update focuses on bug fixes and performance improvements.

This update fixes some error messages which could occur when system is not performing well enough. If you are interested in the details, check out the release notes on [url=https://www.screenbits.com/release-notes ]Screenbits website[/url].

notes.title: January 2022 Update: Improved click effects
notes.content:
January 2022 update improves pointer click effects and brings minor changes to the user interface.

If you use Screenbits to make video tutorials, click effects feature is a useful tool to show mouse clicks to viewers of the tutorial. In the January 2022 update, Screenbits improves pointer click effects to indicate drag & drop and mouse button press/release more accurately. There are also minor changes to the user interface in this update.

If you are interested in the details, check out the release notes on [url=https://www.screenbits.com/release-notes ]Screenbits website[/url].

notes.title: December 2021 Update: New translations for the application
notes.content:
December 2021 update brings new translations for the application. You can now change application language to Chinese Simplified, French, German, Italian, Portuguese (Brazil), Russian and Spanish! 

There are also minor user interface improvements in this update. If you are interested in the details, check out the release notes on [url=https://www.screenbits.com/release-notes ]Screenbits website[/url].

notes.title: October 2021 Update: Improved support for HDR displays and bug fixes
notes.content:
October 2021 update improves support for HDR enabled displays and also fixes a few bugs.

Before the update, some users had to disable HDR color on their display to be able to capture it. This limitation is now removed in the last update. In addition, we have fixed a few bugs in this update. If you are interested in the details, check out the release notes on [url=https://www.screenbits.com/release-notes ]Screenbits website[/url].

notes.title: August 2021 Update: Screenshot Capturing
notes.content:
August 2021 update brings ability to capture screenshots, more screen capturing options and new hotkeys for switching between modes.

You can now capture screenshots from screen, an area on the screen or the capture scene. Use screenshot hotkey (default: Alt+F10) to capture the screen or the capture since. In addition to the hotkey approach, preview, area selection tool and frame now have new screenshot buttons to capture screenshots.

In this new update, you can choose to hide taskbar for your screen recording sessions from screen options. If you have a multi-display setup, a new [i]Active Display[/i] option is available in the list of displays. Using this option, screen capture dynamically switches between displays to capture the display which have mouse pointer on it.

notes.title: July 2021 Update: Audio and Device capture modes
notes.content:
We are happy to announce that the new update (version 7.2.1) now supports new features including individual camera and audio recording. 

Using the device capture mode, you can now record your camera individually just like a camera recorder. Audio capture mode allows you to record audio from system sound and microphone into audio files.

In addition, you can now turn on/off audio capture during recording, and also use push-to-talk mode for input audio capturing.

notes.title: May 2021 Update: New camera options, sound notifications and more
notes.content:
May 2021 update brings new camera overlay features, more sound notifications and options to import and export application settings.

You can now flip camera image from camera options to make it more realistic. You can also choose the format/quality for the camera overlay from a list of supported formats. 

In this new update, sound notifications are played when you pause and resume recording which confirm your action when you use hotkeys in game.

From settings section, new options are available to import and export application settings or reset them to their default. If you use Screenbits on multiple devices, you can now use this feature to export your settings from one device and import it to another one.

notes.title: February 2021 Update: Chroma Key feature
notes.content: February 2021 update brings Chroma Key feature which allows you to easily remove background from camera overlay by choosing a chroma key. In addition to this feature, recording performance is also improved on devices with Intel® Quick Sync Video support.

notes.title: December 2020 Update: Statistics feature
notes.content:
December 2020 update (version 6.2.2) brings statistics feature to Screenbits. This feature provides useful information about the app and current recording session including actual recording frame-rate, health of the output and resource usage of the application.

Stats can be viewed by clicking the stats icon under the recording timer. The icon appears right after recording starts.

notes.title: November 2020 Update: Preview feature
notes.content:
We are happy to announce that the new update (version 6.1.0) now supports Preview feature. This allows you to see how the output looks like before and during recording. 

In addition to this new feature, recording performance has been improved significantly on devices with dedicated GPUs which means smoother video.
